transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Iris (Redwood SE), Laura (Sierra CTO), Miguel (Sierra ML), Priya (Sierra Security), Calvin (Sierra Product)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood - AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the Sierra account. Quick roll call?
[00:22] Laura (Sierra - CTO): Hi, Laura here. Miguel, Priya, Calvin also with me.
[00:27] Miguel (Sierra - ML): Miguel, lead on ML infra.
[00:31] Priya (Sierra - Security): Priya, security and compliance.
[00:36] Maya: Great. Daniel and Iris from our SE org are on — Daniel will cover performance stuff. Goal today is to understand your TTFT needs and where you land on hosted vs Dedicated or Private.
[00:49] Daniel (Redwood - SE): Hi team, quick note: I'll try and keep it pragmatic, we want a path that minimizes ops ramp but meets your compliance.
[01:05] Calvin (Sierra - Product): Primary objective for us is ship a docs-assistant feature into prod by Q2 so TTFT matters. We want low friction trial for PMs and devs.
[01:20] Maya: Makes sense. Two quick qualification questions: what's your current stack for inference and any infra constraints?
[01:35] Miguel: We're on GCP, using Kubernetes for app infra. For models currently experimenting with open models on internal infra, but we don't want to manage all the serving. Latency target is sub-300ms P95 for short prompts, and cost targets are tight — we're a mid-stage startup.
[01:55] Daniel: Sub-300ms P95 is doable with our hosted offering depending on model choice and token length. For higher throughput or stricter P95, customers often consider Dedicated with reserved capacity.
[02:12] Priya: Security side — we need SOC2 alignment, SSO (SAML/Okta), and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) if we get to private. Also data residency possibilities for EU.
[02:28] Iris (Redwood - SE): All of those are supported on the Private path, and Dedicated has enterprise options for SSO and audit logs. Hosted supports SOC2 and encrypted-at-rest keys managed by us, but not customer KMS.
[02:45] Laura: So for a quickstart, we'd prefer hosted to move fast, but we need assurances on logs and minimal data retention — can we scope that?
[02:56] Maya: Yes, our PLG quickstart is hosted-first. We typically give credits, a quickstart repo and a short checklist to get TTFT measured. We'll include instructions to restrict retention and a pointer to the security pack.
[03:13] Miguel: How many free tokens do teams normally get?
[03:17] Maya: We can issue an initial 30k token credit for evaluation, and we can expand on a pilot. That usually gets teams through prototype features.
[03:26] Calvin: 30k — ok. What's typical time-to-first-token in practice? Like minutes? hours?
[03:34] Daniel: For standard SDK flows: minutes to an hour for a dev to hit a sample endpoint and get results. For production-safe integration with SSO and stricter policies, you'd be looking at a few days to a week.
[03:48] Laura: Good. The thing we worry about is cold-start latency and token cost with longer documents — our docs-assistant will ingest 20–30k token contexts for retrieval augmented generation.
[04:03] Daniel: Large context work often uses embeddings+retrieval with chunking; Redwood Optimize recommendations can cut up-front cost. For large context, you can stage a reranker to limit LM token consumption. We also have KV cache behavior to reduce repeated prefix cost, but sometimes transcripts show the engine records it as K-V cash — small transcription errors in our docs, haha.
[04:27] Miguel: (laughs) noted. On the model side, are you curating recommended models for cost vs latency?
[04:33] Iris: Yes, our catalog lists verified profiles: latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality tiers. For your use case we'd likely suggest an instruction-tuned open model quantized for inference; that hits a good cost/latency balance.
[04:54] Priya: Back to security: if we start on hosted and then move to Dedicated or Private, is there a migration path? Data movement concerns us.
[05:06] Maya: Absolutely. We support pinned model versions and export of audit logs and request traces. For Private, you can bring your own KMS and we support VPC peering and on-prem bundles. Migration usually is a phased cutoff where stateful caches are rebuilt but prompts and models are the same.
[05:25] Laura: That sounds promising. Who owns the migration work?
[05:28] Daniel: SE + Customer infra work together. We provide runbooks and tie-breaker checks. For complex deployments we recommend a short Dedicated pilot to validate performance before a Private cutover.
[05:43] Calvin: What's the unit economics for dedicated? We don't have deep pockets so committed spend is scary.
[05:52] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity — typically monthly/annual commits. For pilots, we can low-commit smaller pools and autoscale. Another pattern: start hosted and then once usage justifies it, we help size a dedicated pool to reduce per-token costs.
[06:10] Miguel: Any competitors we should be aware of? We looked at GigaCloud AI and ModelServeX.
[06:16] Maya: Those come up. Compared to GigaCloud AI we emphasize unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private and deeper cost controls like prefix caching and quantization guidance. ModelServeX competes on self-hosted runtimes but often lacks a seamless hosted->private migration path.
[06:34] Priya: Can you share a security pack?
[06:36] Iris: Yes, SE will share our SOC2 kit, SSO integration notes, and KMS/HSM docs. We'll post it to the Confluence link: https://redwood.example.com/security/sierra-pack (placeholder).
[06:53] Laura: Great. For the demo/pilot, we want a short benchmark — tail latency P95 and cost per 1k tokens using our prompt set.
[07:02] Daniel: We'll need your prompts and typical payloads. If you can share a 10–20 sample set, we'll run a mini-benchmark on hosted and simulate Dedicated profiles.
[07:16] Miguel: We can scrub and share a sample set by Monday.
[07:19] Priya: Also we'll share an internal compliance matrix.
[07:23] Maya: Perfect. I'll follow up with the quickstart packet and credits. Daniel, can you outline the benchmark steps?
[07:30] Daniel: Sure — step 1: ingest prompt set and define latency window; step 2: run calls across model candidates with our continuous batching disabled/enabled; step 3: measure P50/P95 and token counts; step 4: provide recommended model/quantization + estimated costs. We'll include code snippets in Python/Node.
[07:54] Calvin: How do we instrument tracing? We use Datadog — can we hook into your tracing?
[07:59] Iris: Yes, we have tracing hooks and can push request traces to your Datadog via logs/OTel integration.
[08:09] Laura: Anything else on pricing? We don't have to lock in yet but need a ballpark for pilot to show finance.
[08:16] Maya: For hosted, it's per-token; I'll include sample cost calculations based on your prompt set. For Dedicated, we'll give ballpark per-token baked into the reserved plan.
[08:29] Miguel: Ok. Timeline: if we get credits and the quickstart today, we can try to have something in our staging by next week.
[08:37] Maya: Sounds good. We'll issue credits today or tomorrow.
[08:41] Priya: Data residency — we have EU customers, so if we process EU data do you have EU-hosted endpoints?
[08:49] Iris: Yes, hosted has EU regions and Private can be deployed within your VPC in EU. We'll note that in the security doc.
[09:01] Laura: Are there guardrails for hallucinations/quality monitoring?
[09:05] Daniel: Yes, Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring, evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We can set a simple eval for the docs-assistant to alert if quality drops.
[09:19] Calvin: Great. Any blockers you foresee?
[09:22] Maya: No major blockers. Biggest near-term ask is the prompt set and compliance matrix. Then we run the mini-benchmark and circle back with results and a proposed pilot size.
[09:34] Laura: Good. Can you summarize next steps?
[09:37] Maya: Sure. I'll summarize: 1) Redwood issues 30k credit and quickstart template; 2) Sierra shares a 10–20 sample prompt set + compliance matrix; 3) SE runs mini-benchmark and returns a recommended model/profile; 4) Redwood sends SOC2/KMS docs and datadog tracing notes.
[09:58] Miguel: Sounds actionable.
[10:02] Priya: We'll aim to send docs by Monday.
[10:06] Maya: Perfect — we'll aim to have benchmark results by end of next week. Any final questions?
[10:13] Laura: None from me. Thanks, everyone.
[10:16] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invite for the benchmark review.

Recap (auto): Quickstart hosted-first with 30k tokens, SE mini-benchmark, security pack to be shared, potential move to Dedicated/Private later.

References shared during call:
- Quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood/quickstart (placeholder)
- Security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/security/sierra-pack
- Mini-benchmark checklist (to be shared): will include code snippets and prompt-run template

End of transcript.
